correctness.rationale: For either Laplacian projector P₂ or P₄ and each edge vector b=e_i−e_j, bᵀP_j b=1: the squared projection onto the alternating unit vector is 1 and the remaining squared norm is 1. Therefore the Bernoulli covariance correction to T(P_j) relative to (I−phL)P_j(I−phL) is exactly p(1−p)h²∑bbᵀ=p(1−p)h²L. This independently yields the stated K and its symmetric Frobenius representation. Independence across rounds gives E||W_k⋯W_1x||²=xᵀT^k(P)x on the mean-zero space; diagonal coefficients are K^k(1,1)ᵀ. For 0<p<1 and h>0 the positive K (positive diagonal from the no-edge event) has a dominant positive Perron vector, so the rate holds for every nonzero mean-zero vector as well as the worst case. At h=0 it is 1; at p=1 it is the maximum of the two deterministic squared modal multipliers. I independently expanded (tr K)²−4 det K, obtained the stated radical, and found det C=16p³(p+3)>0 with C₁₁>0. The smallest eigenvalue of C gives a strictly positive uniform convexity modulus for λ_max(S) in h. The right slope at zero is −4p. For the upper boundary the derivative divided by p is 7p−3+N/√Q; for p≥3/7 it is positive. Below 3/7 the valid squared sign test factors as −16(p−1)(3p−2)(11p²−8p+1), negative below the smaller root and positive above it. This yields the unique optimizing regime at and around the threshold. At p=1 the unique minimizer is the modal crossover h=1/3, with rate 1/9. As a check on the distinction from the one-step objective, at (p,h)=(3/4,2/5) both row sums equal 7/25 but ∂hR=2/5. Only the common-gain family is optimized, with its feasible range [0,1/2]. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Theorem 2.5 of the 2010 paper treats tori to first order in small failure probability, not the exact optimized curve for all p. Its p. 890 weight discussion concerns a separate additive-noise steady-state criterion.
Battilotti–Cacace–d’Angelo Theorems 2–3 concern distributed filtering limits, asymptotic unbiasedness and mean-square boundedness.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An implicit general spectral radius does not by itself classify the constrained optimum; the two-mode reduction and the sign of the boundary derivative supply the additional classification. Neither perturbative tori rates nor filter boundedness dominate an exact all-p optimization.

evidence: The closest catalog descriptions respectively concern a four-node path with a two-message sampling design and single-edge sampling on complete bipartite graphs. K₂,₂ is C₄, but choosing exactly one edge in every round is different from four independently active Bernoulli edges, including no-edge and concurrent-edge events.
The exact general covariance theorem implies a rate for any fixed gain, but no inspected prior statement gives this sign factorization at the stochastic gain cap or the switch it certifies.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The novelty is not the framework or a fixed-gain invocation of it: the optimizer classification comes from additional invariant-space, strong convexity and boundary sign analysis. The same-day matches are distinguished by their stated models, not by their date; their full statements were unavailable.

evidence: Patterson–Bamieh–El Abbadi Theorem 2.3 and the uniform-failure corollary give the exact asymptotic covariance spectral radius for arbitrary connected undirected graphs; set failure probability to 1−p to compare parameters.
Their p. 884 discussion separates the covariance operator from eigenvalues of individual or expected weight matrices.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The rate criterion and methodology are not new. Expected matrix contraction, one-step mean-square energy, and the multiple-round covariance spectral radius are not interchangeable objectives; matching one of the former cannot entail the gain threshold for the latter.

value.rationale: The natural gain-design question is whether to use the maximum nonnegative update or back off to improve long-run mean-square convergence. On C₄ the full reliability law gives a precise boundary and an easily tested example where optimizing a one-step surrogate does not optimize long-run decay. The threshold and proof of uniqueness throughout the feasible range are substantive beyond listing eigenvalues for one graph or one parameter point.
